newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends sharply lower on API data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends sharply lower on API data.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices ended sharply lower Wednesday after oil inventory data showed a bearish build in distillate stocks and ignited profit-taking. "The dam finally broke. People decided to take profits while they can," said Al Lindseth, a trader with GSC Energy.

November heat settled off 2.22 cents to 73.97 cents a gallon. Heating oil stocks have remained at historical lows for months, but the American Petroleum Institute (API) said distillate stocks grew by 1.3 million barrels.
Traders were expecting a much smaller build. Heat stocks still remain a steep 17 million barrels below a year ago.
The sell-off in heating oil took crude lower, with November crude oil ending down 47 cents a barrel at $25.07. November
gasoline ended 0.91 cent a gallon lower at 65.59 cents.

Selling in crude accelerated late session after U.N. Under-Secretary General Chinmaya Gharekhan said he was trying to get visas for three oil monitors from the Dutch-based Saybolt firm to go to Iraq for the pending Iraqi oil-for-food plan.
But, he also said minimum conditions had still not been met to implement the plan.
Gasoline had been firm most of the session as traders sold heating oil to buy gasoline. Dealers said gasoline has bottomed after lagging gains posted by heating oil.
Moreover, traders said gasoline stocks fell in the API report due to seasonal maintenance of refineries, presaging tighter supplies.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
